description.value: An fMRI study comparing brain activation to romantic versus neutral cues in normal-weight historical dieters and nondieters during fasted and fed states.

spans.text: This exploratory study of more broadly-based positive stimuli indicates that there may be neurally-based sensitivities to reward beyond food that is modulated by satiation in those both with and without a history of dieting, and particularly in HDs in the middle temporal gyrus.

value: We hypothesized that, given literature suggesting increased sensitivity to reward in obese or weight-gain prone individuals ( ), HDs may have greater reward response to broadly positive cues.
